16645377: Have just inherited a Halfords Battery Charger from a neighbour. It says on it: ' Most suited for engines over 1800 cc' fast charge 7.5 adc. max battery capacity 110 ah Slow charge 5.5 adc max battery capacity 70 ah Would that mean its not suited for use on my smaller 1600 cc Toyota engine ? Thanks John Rumm 4 years ago As far as I can see the engine size is mostly meaningless - they just seem to be using it as a shortcut to estimate the capacity of the battery - where larger engine will probably need more starting current and have hence have a larger capacity battery fitted. I would guess they are just indicating what size of battery can be fully charged in ~15 hours. So in short, it will be fine. Paul 4 years ago ... If it's anything like my Halfords charger, those rates are to say the least optimistic. it might hit them early on in a charge, but very quickly reduces to well below the peak. I have a cheap (£14) Lidl smart charger. Peak output about 4 amps. But it charges my battery to full quicker than the Halfords one which claims 11 amps peak. Dave Plowman (News 4 years ago ... No. It means that it is fine for your car battery but it would be a bit too hefty for anything much less than a 50Ah battery. C/10 charge rate is 10 hours nominally to fully charged and is about as fast as you really want to push it with a dumb charger. Ballpark rule of thumb is Charge time in hours = 1.1 x Ah of your battery / Charge Current Better measured current output - they are always optimistic about it. ... FWIW my dumb charger is an elderly green Halford special and has no working meter at all. I can judge from the connection spark if it is charging. It's slow and fast rates are 3A and 6A respectively. Dave Plowman (News 4 years ago Ever inserted an ammeter to see the actual charge rate at start and finish of the cycle? A basic dumb one won't charge at its rated max for long. A smart one will charge at near enough constant current - meaning it does the job quicker, like for like in max. output.
